paraphrase: OBQ sequentially fixes weights and uses inverse-curvature compensation of remaining weights. Calibration uses 1024 samples, with ImageNet augmentation and normalization corrections. Table 4 reports asymmetric per-channel 2-bit ResNet50 accuracy 70.71 versus 76.13 float; 4-bit gives 75.72. This is vision/BERT evidence, not ternary Switch validation. A quadratic local optimum does not imply preserved whole-network behavior. Deployment evaluation includes mixed precision/pruning, so a bitrate is not a complete ternary artifact size.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: GPTQ minimizes calibration linear-output error with compensated column quantization, 128-column updates and Cholesky stabilization. Calibration: 128 C4 segments of 2048 tokens. The paper reports group-8 ternary OPT-175B WikiText2 perplexity 9.20 versus 8.34 float, with worse compression than grouped 2-bit. Embedding/head remain FP16. Current unpinned quant.py uses {xmin,0,xmax}; common ±alpha requires symmetry. Published ternary language quality neither establishes 1% expert RMS nor exact generations or native CPU speed.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: AdaRound optimizes soft floor/ceiling choices through layer reconstruction plus an annealed rounding penalty. It uses 1024 unlabeled ImageNet images, Adam, 10000 iterations and batch 32. Table 2's relaxed local objective improves ResNet18 full-model accuracy over nearest rounding, but this is a vision demonstration of learned rounding, not ternary pretrained-language evidence. The quantization grid and layer-local target restrict the attainable solution; no strict common-scale ternary storage or native deployment proof is provided.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: BRECQ reconstructs blocks using adaptive rounding and a Fisher-weighted objective; calibration uses 1024 ImageNet images and Adam. First/last layers stay 8-bit. Table 2 reports 2-bit MobileNetV2 accuracy 59.67 versus 72.49 float; lower reconstruction error does not eliminate quality loss. Section 3.1 explicitly discusses whole-network calibration overfitting. These are integer-grid vision experiments, not strict ternary LLM proof. Mixed precision, activation ranges and boundary layers must be included in deployment accounting.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: OmniQuant learns clipping and equivalent scale/shift transformations through block reconstruction. It uses 128 WikiText2 segments of 2048 tokens, batch 1, AdamW, 20 epochs or 40 for W2A16; Llama weight-only enables clipping only. Table 1's W2 group-128 Llama2-7B perplexity is 11.06 versus 5.47 float. Uniform 2-bit has four levels, not three. Fused transforms reduce runtime overhead, but strict ternary artifact storage and original Switch fidelity are untested.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: SignRound jointly optimizes rounding and clipping using signed gradient descent over block reconstruction, typically 200 steps. Calibration uses 512 pile-10k segments of 2048 tokens, with some 70B comparisons reduced to 128 because of NaNs/cost. Evaluation includes whole-model perplexity and eleven zero-shot tasks. Claimed near-lossless cases are principally 4-bit; relative 2-bit improvements do not imply full-precision recovery. Its integer alphabets, optional grouping and tuned ranges are not strict ternary codes.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: QuIP combines quadratic-proxy adaptive rounding with randomized orthogonal incoherence transforms. It calibrates on 128 C4 segments of 2048 tokens, propagating quantized-block inputs. Improved 2-bit results depend on model size and transforms; the theoretical guarantees concern proxy error, not identical language behavior. Table 4 reports OPT66B per-token times 81ms versus OPTQ 53ms on A6000. Four-level transformed weights and stored transforms are not an original-coordinate common-scale ternary representation.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: QuIP# uses randomized Hadamard transforms and E8P vector codebooks, not scalar ternary. Hessians use 6144 RedPajama sequences at native context length. Optional block tuning uses 256 training/128 validation sequences for five epochs; additional end-to-end tuning is distinct. Llama2-70B costs exclude Hessian generation: under 10 GPU-hours without tuning, around 100 with tuning. Appendix F1 counts a shared 1KiB codebook and sign-vector overhead. Ablations separate codebook, transform and tuning effects.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: QTIP replaces vector rounding with trellis-coded high-dimensional quantization inside BlockLDLQ; its decoded values are not ternary. Hessian budgets include 6144x2048 RedPajama sequences for Llama1/2 and 4096x8192 for Llama3. Pure computed-code arms omit tuning; hybrid arms tune codebook and unquantized weights. Hybrid codebook is 2KiB. Quantizing the first value projection can catastrophically collapse Llama3-70B zero-shot performance. Published GPU throughput depends on specialized decoding and does not establish local CPU performance.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: AQLM approximates weight groups by sums of learned vector codewords, with discrete code search, gradient codebook optimization and joint block reconstruction. Calibration commonly uses 8M RedPajama tokens; end-to-end tuning is separately reported. Appendix E shows Llama2-7B 2.3-bit perplexity improving 6.994→6.267 as samples grow 128→4096. Code indices, books, scales and retained parameters count toward effective bits. Additive codebooks supply richer values than one ternary plane; their success does not rescue an unchanged scalar alphabet.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: GPTVQ combines activation-aware EM codebooks, Hessian compensation, optional codebook updates and codebook compression. It uses 128 WikiText2 training sequences of 2048 tokens and typically 100 EM iterations. Appendix Table 8 reports 2.125-bpv Llama1-7B perplexity 9.64 for 2D versus 5.68 float. Codebook overhead is explicitly budgeted at 0.125 or 0.25 bits/value. Table 1's mobile throughput includes dedicated decoding; vector codebook indices do not denote scalar ternary values.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: SpQR preserves sensitive outliers in FP16 and quantizes other weights with compressed scales/zeros. Calibration uses RedPajama or RefinedWeb, according to model family. Table 1's near-1%-perplexity Llama65B arm uses 4.71 effective bits versus nominal 3/4; at 3.90 bits WikiText2 rises 3.53→3.68. Outliers additionally cost roughly 32 bits each plus row pointers. Specialized sparse decoding yields GPU gains; ordinary sparse multiplication is not faster. This mixed format is not pure ternary.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: CoreQ separates reachable and unreachable propagated input mismatch, computes a closed-form correction, and performs successive rounding with optional bounded beam search. It uses 128 C4 samples of 2048 tokens and five calibration seeds; time includes non-GPU overhead on H200. Finite calibration makes both uncorrected and fully corrected targets unreliable. Table 1's symmetric 3-bit Llama3-8B per-channel perplexity improves 24.65→16.48, still a relative comparison. Integer-grid evidence does not prove a ternary nonlinear FFN can absorb mismatch.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: SLQ distinguishes task recovery from distribution fidelity, using EAR as coupling agreement. Mixed per-layer asymmetric GPTQ precision uses 512 calibration samples and Shapley/ILP allocation. Reported task-preserving points span 3.3–4.7 effective bits; distribution-preserving points 5.0–6.6. QTIP4 on Llama3.3-70B recovers 99.9% task means yet EAR is 0.9544. Metrics use top-10 calibration tokens, and task search uses benchmark anchoring: these are not untouched-heldout distribution proofs. Results support scoped fidelity distinctions, not a universal ternary impossibility.
applicability: Comparative method evidence; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.

paraphrase: INQ repeatedly partitions pretrained CNN weights, quantizes/freezes one group, and retrains the remaining group. Targets are powers of two or zero; its 2-bit arm is ternary. ImageNet has 1.2M labeled training images. The ternary ResNet18 run uses ten cumulative partition stages and 30 epochs; top-1 error increases 31.73%→33.98%. Random partition underperforms magnitude-based partition at 5-bit. This closely matches progressive conversion without training from scratch, but it is supervised recovery, not calibration-only LLM evidence.
applicability: Historical progressive-conversion precedent; not independent replication or proof of the local research goal.
